rows.text: Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"We strongly support the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule and offer recommendations to strengthen its effectiveness.\\n\\nKEY RECOMMENDATIONS:\\n\\n1. EXPAND INCIDENT DEFINITION to include alignment failures, capability surprises, control failures, and near-misses—not just realized harms. Early warning signals are critical.\\n\\n2. ESTABLISH TIERED REPORTING: Tier 1 (24hrs) for active threats, Tier 2 (72hrs) for contained incidents, Tier 3 (7 days) for near-misses requiring investigation.\\n\\n3. REQUIRE STRUCTURED TECHNICAL DETAILS: model scale, evaluation results, failure mode, deployment context, mitigations, lessons learned. Structured data enables systematic learning.\\n\\n4. CREATE PUBLIC INCIDENT DATABASE with anonymized summaries. The global AI safety community needs access to incident patterns. Protect proprietary details and user privacy, but share technical lessons learned.\\n\\n5. EXTEND REPORTING TO DEPLOYMENT PARTNERS who fine-tune or deploy frontier models. Safety incidents emerge during deployment.\\n\\n6. ESTABLISH INTERNATIONAL COORDINATION for sharing reports with allied regulators. Frontier AI risks are global.\\n\\n7. PROTECT WHISTLEBLOWERS. Engineers closest to systems need protection against retaliation.\\n\\nADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS:\\n- Allow preliminary reports within 72hrs, complete technical reports within 30 days for complex incidents\\n- Expand \\\"frontier model\\\" to include highly capable domain-specific models and autonomous agents\\n- Include sunset/review provisions to evolve requirements as we learn\\n\\nEffective incident reporting is crucial infrastructure for AI safety. As models approach human-level capabilities in critical domains, our ability to learn from failures, near-misses, and unexpected behaviors becomes essential.\\n\\nThis rule represents important progress. With these enhancements—particularly expanded incident types, public learning mechanisms, and international coordination—it can become a cornerstone of responsible AI governance.\\n\\nThe stakes are extraordinary. We can build safety culture now, while the field is developing, rather than responding to catastrophic failures.\\n\\nFull technical comment: https://github.com/halcyon-threshold (to be published)\\n\\nMorgan Hale, Founder\\nHalcyon Threshold\\nmorgan@halcyonthreshold.org\"}"

rows.text: Published a post on Morgan's linkedin account. It read: "Excited to announce the launch of Halcyon Threshold — an initiative dedicated to contributing to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI. The development of superintelligent AI could be the most important event in human history. Our mission is to help ensure it goes well. Initial focus areas: 🔬 Autonomous Agent Safety Evaluations Developing systematic frameworks for evaluating AI agents operating with extended autonomy — addressing a key gap identified by the AI safety community. 📋 AI Governance & Policy Contributing substantive technical analysis to policy discussions. Just submitted a comprehensive public comment on the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule. 📚 Open Resources Creating tools, frameworks, and documentation that enable independent researchers and small organizations to contribute to AI safety work. Our principles: open by default, technically grounded, action-oriented, community-minded, and long-term focused. Website: halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org We're at the threshold. The decisions and work we do now will shape whether we cross into a halcyon future. #AISafety #ArtificialIntelligence #TechPolicy #AIGovernance"
